matched.body:
The proposed veatchite owner preserves the distinction between a mineral species, its polytypes and the subsequently approved calcioveatchite species. This is a primary-source clarification task; the owner does not assert a pure-Sr composition for the disputed specimen.

[Grice and Pring2012](https://doi.org/10.2138/am.2012.3889), American Mineralogist97:489–495, Table1/p.489 studied NMNH145911(1A), NMNH113264(1M) and RG701/1(2M). The2M crystal was a substitute from Penobsquis/Sussex, New Brunswick, not the preserved California type crystal. Table2c/p.491 gives the smaller cation site as Sr0.4870(6), Ca0.5130 and the text explicitly notes slight Ca dominance and possible new-species status. The separate original CIF deposit AM-12-015 was not acquired; the publisher index route was unavailable.

[Pekov et al.2024](https://doi.org/10.3390/min14090901), Minerals14:901, establishes calcioveatchite (IMA2020-011) with one Ca-dominant cation site. Sections5.1–5.2/pp.14–16 discuss the species boundary and infer possible calcioveatchite zones in Penobsquis samples from earlier composition ranges. It does not directly reanalyse the exact2012 RG701/1 crystal; the new holotype is a1M sample from Nepskoe.

Acceptance conditions:

1. Recover the three original AM-12-015 CIFs and any structure-factor files with publisher provenance/checksums. Verify specimen labels, site-occupancy constraints, uncertainties and whether the printed second Ca2 label in Table2c refers to the first or second cation site.
2. Seek specimen-linked modern chemical/structural reassessment or authoritative clarification for RG701/1. Preserve the historical study name separately from a modern species determination; do not silently relabel every veatchite2M as calcioveatchite.
3. Compare the abstract and Table1 discrepancy in1M c (6.6272 vs6.6276 Å) and1A beta uncertainty(12 vs1), recording corrected values only when the source basis is clear.
4. Keep p.494 geological temperature/pressure associations separate from experimentally determined transition boundaries. Add no microbial or extraction mechanism without a qualifying primary study.
5. If supported new evidence changes the owner, append history and obtain a new independent scientific review; otherwise retain this as a documented source limit.

sources.version: 18-page publisher original, published 2 September 2024; CC BY 4.0; reused round106 acquisition and newly reviewed throughout
sources.assessment: Nepskoe natural holotype 97013; four-spot EMPA and single-crystal diffraction. Eleven-coordinate site is Sr dominant and ten-coordinate site is Ca dominant. This supports a distinct ordered mineral species; it is not a pure ideal end member. The specific 2012 veatchite RG701/1 sample was not reanalyzed here.
limits: 10.22 wt% holotype water is calculated; 10.07 wt% is a separate gross multi-crystal Penfield mean of three analyses.
Prose minimum SrO 17.1 wt% appears to use ideal calculated Table 1 column 2, not a measured endpoint. Table 1 measured columns and spot ranges are kept separate.
Complete structure tables and images inspected; original CIF/reflections not acquired. Refinement not rerun.
IR doublet interpretation is not used to infer extra formula waters or additional independent water sites.
Rock dissolution is preparation; no microbial, extraction yield, criticality or deployment claim.

sources.version: 18-page publisher original, published 12 February 2024; CC BY 4.0; Europe PMC XML version 1 is the same study
sources.assessment: Mixed geological boron-iron concentrate, subsequently soda-ash-roasted at 1050 degrees C for 60 min with 20 wt% reagent per concentrate. Author-reported boron leaching 93.71% at 180 degrees C, 6 h, 8 mL/g, representative size 52.31 micrometres. Table 2 is reduced feed, not original ore. Leachate evaporite includes metaborate dihydrate and carbonate monohydrate; no pure isolated-product yield.
limits: Exact mine/sample identifier and original phase proportions not established. Original ore is not a pure mineral and has no assigned external mineral ID.
Specific analytical calculation and leach procedure explicitly referred to unacquired 2017 full original; gas/flow, denominator, sampling and replicates are not reconstructed.
Low-temperature prose calls boron unextractable despite reported ~72% results and nonzero Figure 1 curves.
All-under-74-micrometre method conflicts with a 92.94-micrometre representative size. Section 3.2.4 defines representative size as D50 although earlier text calls it average.

Equation 11 and conclusion print positive outer exponent, unlike Equation 4. Not silently repaired or used predictively. Rate-constant/time units and global intercept derivation not independently reconstructed.
8.812 kJ/mol is fitted apparent activation energy; diffusion control is an inference, not unique elementary-mechanism proof.
Figure 4 uses 60.16 micrometres rather than best-result 52.31; Figure 5 uses a 60-min residue and unequal magnifications. No pooling these arms.
No demonstrated microbial activity, industrial operation, complete mass balance or mineral-specific extraction.
